target_customer: Small and growing merchants in Singapore and Southeast Asia that sell online and in person
problem: SMEs in Southeast Asia needed one account to accept cards, PayNow, QR and local wallets across online, in-person and cross-border sales without enterprise integrations.
business_model: payments take rate per transaction plus SaaS add-ons (POS, invoicing, payouts)
product_category: SME payments gateway and payments infrastructure

founders.name: Aditya Haripurkar
founders.background_notes: No education or employer found in sources opened (YC page, TechCrunch, DealStreetAsia).

founders.name: Nitin Muthyala
prior_employers: a Singapore cybersecurity startup (unnamed on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page; CTO title per DealStreetAsia 2022-06-02.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payment aggregation over cards, PayNow and wallets with plugins for Shopify and WooCommerce is standard engineering, with licensing and reconciliation as the hard parts; the MAS major payment institution licence came only in 2024.

defensibility.rationale: Early on the product was an aggregator of third party rails, which many gateways offer; later licences in six markets and merchant integrations add some protection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large gateways stayed in market; HitPay itself still operates independently as of the YC page and 2024 news. Rivals named here come from undated 2026 comparison pages, so treat as context only.

market_need_then: SME merchants in Southeast Asia were digitising sales and wanted local payment methods such as PayNow and wallets in one place; the company says more than 10,000 merchants used it by mid 2022 (fintechnews.sg).

branding.domain_note: Uses hitpayapp.com as primary domain, not the exact hitpay.com; no acquisition story found.

identity.logo: wordmark with brand colours described by the company as professional, trustworthy and modern

brand_strength.rationale: Only a brand guidelines page and aggregator pages were found; no independent press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: HitPay is active and growing: it joined YC in Summer 2021, raised a 15.75 million dollar Series A led by Tiger Global in May 2022, and won an in-principle MAS licence in February 2024 followed by a full major payment institution licence reported in June 2024. Its edge is local payment method coverage for SMEs and regulatory licences in several markets; no shutdown or acquisition was found.
notes: Series A stated by HitPay, TechCrunch, DealStreetAsia and fintechnews.sg at 15.75 to 15.8 million; a Preqin entry says 44 million with Rocket Internet, unverified and ignored. Competitor list left empty: searches returned only undated 2026 vendor comparison pages (HitPay, Airwallex, Stripe), nothing dated near the 2021 batch. Seed rounds before 2022 not found.
